comment: Canonical-JSON conformance fixture (SPEC.md 5.3). Canonical JSON is RFC 8785 (JCS) — ECMAScript number serialization, minimal string escaping, UTF-16 code unit key sort — with AgentMesh's two rules stated in 5.3: absent members are omitted (never serialized as null), and null, where present, is a value distinct from absent. Every vector's expected bytes were derived from RFC 8785's rules and Appendix B, then confirmed byte-identical against the TS SDK's canonicalJSON (2026-07-27, zero TS changes needed) before the Rust SDK was held to them. Tests: sdk-typescript/__tests__/unit/canonical-json.test.ts and sdk-rust/tests/canonical_json.rs. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY: a failing implementation is wrong; change a vector only with a spec change alongside, because a byte change here is a signature break for every envelope in flight.
encoding: Each vector: parse `input_json` (raw JSON text) with the implementation's JSON parser, canonicalize the value, and compare against `canonical` — the exact canonical text; the signed bytes are its UTF-8 encoding. `number_bits` rows are RFC 8785 Appendix B: the big-endian hex IEEE-754 bit pattern of a double and its required serialization; they enter the pipeline as f64, not as JSON text, so they also pin values a lossy parser could never reach.

vectors.name: int_2p53
vectors.note: RFC 8785 Appendix B row 4340000000000000.

vectors.name: int_2p53_plus_1
vectors.note: JCS numbers are IEEE-754 doubles (RFC 8785 3.2.2.3): 2^53+1 is not representable and rounds to 2^53. A sender needing exact integers beyond 2^53 must carry them as strings (I-JSON, RFC 7493).

vectors.name: int_u64_max
vectors.note: 2^64-1 as a double is 2^64; ECMAScript integer notation applies up to 1e21.

vectors.name: float_1e21
vectors.note: First magnitude serialized in exponent form; note the explicit plus sign. RFC 8785 Appendix B row 444b1ae4d6e2ef50.

vectors.name: float_1e20
vectors.note: Below the 1e21 threshold: plain integer digits, NOT 1e+20.

vectors.name: float_below_1e21
vectors.note: RFC 8785 Appendix B row 444b1ae4d6e2ef4f.

vectors.name: float_1e-6
vectors.note: Smallest magnitude still in decimal notation, NOT 1e-6. RFC 8785 Appendix B row 3eb0c6f7a0b5ed8d.

vectors.name: float_1e-7
vectors.note: First magnitude below 1e-6: exponent form, no plus sign on negative exponents.

vectors.name: float_9999e-7
vectors.note: RFC 8785 Appendix B row 3eb0c6f7a0b5ed8c.

vectors.name: float_long_double
vectors.note: RFC 8785 Appendix B row 41b3de4355555554: 17 significant digits needed to round-trip.

vectors.name: float_long_double_shorter
vectors.note: RFC 8785 Appendix B row 41b3de4355555555: the neighbouring double needs only 16.

vectors.name: float_integral
vectors.note: An integral double serializes without .0 — there is no float/int distinction in ECMAScript.

vectors.name: negative_zero_float
vectors.note: RFC 8785 Appendix B row 8000000000000000: IEEE negative zero serializes as 0 (ECMAScript Number::toString), the sign is dropped.

vectors.name: float_min_subnormal
vectors.note: RFC 8785 Appendix B row 0000000000000001.

vectors.name: float_max_double
vectors.note: RFC 8785 Appendix B row 7fefffffffffffff.

vectors.name: float_small_negative
vectors.note: RFC 8785 Appendix B row becbf647612f3696.

vectors.name: string_control_chars
vectors.note: Controls without a shorthand escape use lowercase \u00hh.

vectors.name: string_shorthand_escapes
vectors.note: The five controls with two-character escapes MUST use them.

vectors.name: string_vertical_tab
vectors.note: U+000B has no shorthand in JSON.

vectors.name: string_quote_backslash
vectors.note: Only quote and reverse solidus are escaped among printables.

vectors.name: string_solidus
vectors.note: Solidus is NOT escaped, even when the input escaped it.

vectors.name: string_del_and_u0080
vectors.note: Escaping stops at U+001F: DEL and C1 controls are emitted raw.

vectors.name: string_line_separators
vectors.note: U+2028/U+2029 are raw in JSON (they only need escaping in JavaScript source).

vectors.name: string_non_bmp
vectors.note: A surrogate pair in the input is one non-BMP character, emitted as raw UTF-8.

vectors.name: string_precomposed
vectors.note: No normalization and no gratuitous escaping: the code point as sent.

vectors.name: sort_empty_key
vectors.note: The empty string sorts before everything.

vectors.name: sort_digits_before_letters
vectors.note: Plain code-unit order: "10" < "2", uppercase before lowercase. Not numeric, not locale-aware.

vectors.name: sort_rfc_example
vectors.input_json: {"\u20ac":"Euro Sign","\r":"Carriage Return","\ufb33":"Hebrew Letter Dalet With Dagesh","1":"One","\ud83d\ude00":"Emoji: Grinning Face","\u0080":"Control","\u00f6":"Latin Small Letter O With Diaeresis"}
vectors.canonical: {"\r":"Carriage Return","1":"One","":"Control","ö":"Latin Small Letter O With Diaeresis","€":"Euro Sign","😀":"Emoji: Grinning Face","דּ":"Hebrew Letter Dalet With Dagesh"}
vectors.note: RFC 8785 3.2.3's own example, verbatim.

vectors.name: sort_beyond_bmp
vectors.note: THE sort vector that separates UTF-16 code unit order from UTF-8 byte order: U+1F600's high surrogate 0xD83D sorts before U+FB00, while its UTF-8 bytes (F0...) sort after (EF...).

vectors.name: member_null
vectors.note: null, where present, is a value and is serialized. Compare member_absent: different bytes, different signature.

vectors.name: member_absent
vectors.note: A member the sender did not set MUST NOT be serialized as null — it is simply not there. Compare member_null.

vectors.name: parent_span_id_root
vectors.note: The envelope schema itself uses an explicit null: trace.parent_span_id is null for root spans (SPEC.md 5.2) and those bytes are signed.

vectors.name: nested_mixed
vectors.note: Sorting recurses into every object; arrays keep their order.

vectors.name: array_order_kept
vectors.note: Arrays are never sorted.
